title: Segregated audit proxy and customer-storage rotation strategy for private deployments
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Provide a hardened, tenant-segregated audit forwarding agent and rotation strategy that enables Private/VPC/on-prem customers to ship audit logs to customer-managed object stores (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) while preserving encryption ownership, retention/rotation controls, and tamper-evidence. This ticket scopes: (1) design and implement a lightweight audit proxy process suitable for Private and on-prem bundles; (2) define signed-upload and key handshake patterns that preserve CMEK/HSM ownership; (3) define retention/rotation and manifesting strategy for efficient egress and legal-hold support; (4) operational runbook and rollout plan for Dedicated->Private parity.
background: Customers operating in regulated environments require direct control of their audit artifacts. Existing hosted audit ships either push to Redwood-managed buckets or rely on heavy VPNs. For Private/VPC and on-prem we need a predictable, auditable, and minimal-trust path that: uses customer-managed keys where required, supports resumable large uploads, provides per-tenant prefixing and integrity verification, and integrates with RBAC v2/SSO events so account actions correlate to exported records.
decision_log:
Design decisions so far:
- Use a two-mode forwarder: Agent mode (runs in customer env) and Proxy mode (optional in VPC) to avoid opening inbound firewall rules.
- All uploads use pre-signed, short-lived URLs or brokered multipart uploads; content is additionally encrypted with an envelope key generated by Redwood forwarder and wrapped by customer CMEK when available.
- Use per-batch manifest files that list object keys, sequence numbers and HMACs for tamper-evidence; manifests are signed by the forwarder and stored alongside logs.
- Retention/rotation: support lifecycle policies + explicit manifesting to enable legal-hold snapshots. Rotation of credentials is handled by a pluggable provider pattern (IAM role, service principal, SAS token).
- Integrity: each upload includes a SHA-256 checksum and forwarder-attestation header; on receipt, the customer's bucket lifecycle or function can verify and generate an acknowledgement for replay tracking.
Trade-offs considered:
- Direct streaming into customer bucket reduces latency but complicates replay/attribution; we chose brokered upload with manifesting for stronger auditability.
- Envelope encryption adds CPU overhead but enables us to preserve chain-of-trust when customer CMEK is unavailable; acceptance: small CPU trade for stronger guarantees.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Agent can run in offline/private networks and deliver audit batches to customer-managed bucket via pre-signed/multipart upload pattern.
2) Manifests are generated per-batch and include sequence IDs, SHA-256 sums, forwarder signature, and optional SAML/SSO session correlation metadata.
3) CMEK wrap/unwrap handshake documented and automated for AWS/GCP/Azure flows; when CMEK not available, envelope key path is used and logged as 'no-cmek'.
4) Admin console shows per-tenant last-exported offset, last-successful-upload timestamp, and bucket/object path.
5) Test coverage: unit + integration test that simulates network interruption and resumes a multipart upload; CI verifies manifest verification logic.
6) Security review completed and approval from Security and Compliance owners documented.
implementation_notes:
Architecture sketch:
- Forwarder agent (go): tail local audit queue -> batch -> sign manifest -> persist encrypted chunk -> attempt upload.
- Upload modes: (A) Brokered pre-signed URL step: agent requests short-lived PUT URL from control-plane proxy that performs STS/assume-role or issues signed SAS token; (B) Direct IAM path for on-prem with static creds stored only in customer KMS wrapper.
- Key lifecycle: forwarder generates ephemeral envelope key per-batch (AES-256-GCM), wraps with customer KMS key via Encrypt/WrapKey APIs. Encrypted envelope stored in object metadata.
- Tamper evidence & attribution: manifests signed with forwarder private key. Signing keys rotate using a simple KMS-backed schedule.
- Backpressure/durability: local durable queue with configurable high-water mark; metrics expose queued bytes and oldest-record-age.
- Admin controls: console allows read-only preview of manifest indices and revoke of forwarding tokens; RBAC v2 policy gates responsibility to disable/enable exports.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Credential leakage on misconfigured agents. Mitigation: require a device-bound credential (instance identity) for ephemeral STS tokens; default to short-lived tokens and document secure provisioning.
Risk: Longer stalls causing local disk bloat. Mitigation: local pruning policy and warn at 75% disk usage, plus alerting in Console.
Risk: Customer-side lifecycle policies inadvertently delete manifests. Mitigation: recommend prefixing manifests to a reserved path and provide a small lifecycle template for customers.
Risk: CMEK handshake complexity across clouds. Mitigation: provide tested reference flows for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and fallbacks; include an interop test harness in the on-prem bundle.

notes: Implementation should strive for minimal required customer network configuration. For VPC customers the recommended flow is Deploy proxy in customer subnet and use mutual-TLS between proxy and agent. For air-gapped on-prem, support an offline bundle that writes to local NFS or SMB which ops can rsync to customer bucket using separate orchestration. We will provide an 'attestation' CLI that verifies manifests locally before upload.

post_deploy_monitoring:
- Metrics: forwarder.upload.success_count, forwarder.upload.fail_count, forwarder.queue_depth_bytes, forwarder.last_uploaded_offset.
- Alerts: >5 failed attempts in 1m => Pager.
- Daily export health job that compares Console-known offsets to bucket manifests and flags divergence.
